en: The Banaue Rice Terraces use the inclined plane simple machine to help farmers carry heavy harvests up the mountain with less effort.
The deep treads on a Philippine jeepney's tires increase friction against the road to prevent the vehicle from slipping.
Gravity pulls the water of Pagsanjan Falls downward, causing it to accelerate as it drops from the high cliffs.
The black sand found on the beaches of Ilocos contains magnetite, a natural magnetic mineral that can attract iron filings.
The La Mesa Dam hydroelectric power plant generates electricity by using flowing water to spin large turbines connected to generators.
Water droplets in the mist of Maria Cristina Falls refract sunlight, splitting white light into a visible rainbow spectrum.
The historic bells of the Manila Cathedral produce sound waves by vibrating the surrounding air when struck by the clapper.
A traditional clay palayok pot conducts heat directly from the charcoal fire to cook the Filipino dish sinigang evenly.
A carabao converts the chemical energy stored in digested cogon grass into kinetic energy to plow the rice field.
The traditional wooden tool used to crack Bicol pili nuts acts as a second-class lever to easily break the hard shell.
Hot air inside the Mayon Volcano's crater rises through convection, carrying ash and gases high into the atmosphere.
The electric guitar pickups used by Filipino rock bands contain magnets and wire coils that convert string vibrations into electrical signals.
